Manual OpenCode Installation on WSL

https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/releases/download/v1.18.4/opencode-linux-x64.tar.gz

I encountered the same issue and found that the root cause is the installation path.

The OpenCode Desktop app expects the binary to be located at:

text
~/.local/bin/opencode
When installed via npm install --global opencode-ai, the binary is placed in a different location (e.g., /usr/local/bin/opencode), which the Desktop app does not recognize — even though it works fine from the CLI.

Solution: Manually install OpenCode to the expected path.

bash
# Download the Linux binary for your architecture from:
# https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/releases

cd /tmp
curl -LO https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/releases/download/v1.18.4/opencode-linux-x64.tar.gz

# Extract and install to ~/.local/bin/
mkdir -p ~/.local/bin
tar -xzf opencode-linux-x64.tar.gz
mv opencode ~/.local/bin/
chmod +x ~/.local/bin/opencode
After placing the binary at ~/.local/bin/opencode, restart WSL (wsl --shutdown) and reopen the Desktop app. The version check should now pass.

This worked for me — hope it helps!

This is taking the wrong path for the direct MiniMax provider. `minimax/MiniMax-M3` is wired through `@ai-sdk/anthropic` to MiniMax's Anthropic-compatible Messages API, so OpenAI-style `reasoningEffort: "xhigh"` does not control this route. Likewise, changing the direct route from `thinking.type: "adaptive"` to `"enabled"` as proposed in #35181 would be incorrect.

MiniMax's current Anthropic-compatible API documentation is explicit:

- omit `thinking`: thinking is off
- `thinking: { "type": "adaptive" }`: thinking is on
- `thinking: { "type": "disabled" }`: thinking is off

Docs: https://platform.minimax.io/docs/api-reference/text-anthropic-api

MiniMax M3 does not expose meaningful reasoning-effort tiers on this route; it is an on/off toggle. Even MiniMax's separate Responses API says `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, and `high` are accepted only for compatibility and **do not tune reasoning depth** (`xhigh` is not supported): https://platform.minimax.io/docs/api-reference/responses-create

OpenCode already uses `adaptive`/`disabled` for direct MiniMax M3 and explicitly enables `adaptive` on the Anthropic path. The actual bug was provider-specific: NVIDIA and Lilac expose M3 through OpenAI-compatible proxies whose toggle is `chat_template_kwargs.thinking_mode`. That is fixed narrowly in #38330 by returning those native bodies as ordinary variants for NVIDIA/Lilac, while preserving direct MiniMax's existing `adaptive`/`disabled` behavior. There is no request rewriting or global MiniMax behavior change.

Closing as not planned because the proposed configuration and #35181 are not valid fixes for the direct MiniMax route.

This was fixed by #31426 and shipped in OpenCode v1.17.0. That PR enabled `thinking: { "type": "adaptive" }` for MiniMax M3 on the direct Anthropic-compatible route and added the `none`/`thinking` variants. This report was filed against v1.16.2, before the fix was released.

The custom provider configuration in the report also uses `https://api.minimax.io` as its Anthropic `baseURL`; MiniMax documents `https://api.minimax.io/anthropic`, and OpenCode's built-in provider already uses the correct Anthropic endpoint. The built-in provider should be used without overriding that URL.

For completeness, #38330 later corrected MiniMax M3 variant bodies specifically for NVIDIA and Lilac. It intentionally preserves the direct MiniMax behavior added by #31426.

Closing as completed.

+1 — concrete local-model use case to add weight to this request.

**Setup:** I run `google/gemma-4-e4b` locally on macOS via LM Studio, connected to OpenCode Desktop as a custom `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` provider. Gemma 4 E2B/E4B natively understand audio and video, and the local backends are catching up: llama.cpp already merged Gemma 4 audio encoder support ([ggml-org/llama.cpp#21421](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/21421)) and routes `input_audio` content blocks on its OpenAI-compatible `/v1/chat/completions` endpoint; vLLM supports audio for E2B/E4B plus video via frame extraction.

**Current blocker is on the OpenCode side:** V2 prompt attachments and the `read` tool only pass UTF-8 text and PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP images to the model — audio/video files never reach the provider, so even a fully audio-capable local backend cannot be exercised from the TUI/Desktop. I verified this end-to-end: image input works (configured `modalities: { input: [text, image] }` in `opencode.json`), while an `input_audio` test succeeds at the backend level but there is no way to attach the file in OpenCode.

**Suggestion:** when extending attachment media types, gate them behind the existing per-model `modalities` config (e.g. `input: [text, image, audio, video]`) so text-only/vision-only models stay protected, and surface a clear error like the current image path does. This would unlock fully-local multimodal workflows (meeting transcription, video analysis) with zero cloud dependency.

I have a specific case that makes this worse: **custom tools that dispatch long-running commands via HTTP** (e.g., a gateway tool that runs test suites on the host).

The issue is that the TUI only re-renders tool state when it receives part updates from the processor. Built-in tools like `bash` emit incremental stdout/stderr updates, which trigger re-renders and the timer recalculates. Custom tools produce no intermediate events between `tool-call` (running) and `tool-result` (completed) — so the TUI never re-renders and the timer never appears.

For a test suite that runs 10-15 minutes, the tool sits in `running` state with zero visual feedback. I can't tell if it's working or stuck.

The `time.start` timestamp is already set on the tool part — the TUI just needs a periodic refresh (e.g., 1s) for any part with `state.status === "running"`, regardless of whether it emits incremental output.

## More Detailed Proposal

OpenCode currently initializes its TUI renderer with hard-coded `targetFps: 60`, while leaving OpenTUI's separate `maxFps` cap at its default.
See: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/tui/src/app.tsx

On systems where an animation or spinner keeps the renderer live, lowering both values **substantially** reduces CPU usage (the app is internally walking a huge scene graph 60 times per second) as well as remote-terminal traffic.

Something as simple as an environment variable would suffice, e.g.:

`OPENCODE_TUI_FPS=10 opencode`

## Unsupported workaround: Binary patch OpenCode TUI to throttle FPS

_(targets binary in official Docker image `ghcr.io/anomalyco/opencode`)_

While native FPS configuration is being considered...
I developed a binary-patch workaround that makes a copy of the `opencode` binary with both `targetFps` and `maxFps` set as specified. You can easily make separate binaries for different uses, e.g. `opencode-fps-30`, `opencode-fps-10`, `opencode-fps-1`, etc.

At some point in the future when OpenCode changes the relevant code, this patch will no longer work (but it should fail gracefully as opposed to created a corrupt binary).

This patch is provided for experimentation, with no warranties. Review the script before running it.



```js
#!/usr/bin/env node

/**
 * opencode-fps-patch.js -
 * This script creates a modified copy of the `opencode` binary,
 * but with a different target and max FPS "patched" (a.k.a. hacked) in.
 * 
 * 
 * ## Background
 * 
 *  - OpenCode is a great open-source TUI coding agent.
 *  - OpenCode TUI, by default, runs and renders at 60 FPS, hard-coded.
 *  - Even a basic animation or spinner that keeps the renderer live wastes
 *    _immense_ amounts of CPU cycles, energy, and network bandwidth.
 *  - There is no option to change FPS in the application itself.
 *  - There are multiple open and closed issues about this, but no resolutions.
 * 
 * 
 * Main related issues:
 *  - https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/13817
 *  - https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/19466
 * 
 * Possibly related issues:
 *  - https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/811
 *  - https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/6172
 *  - https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/11119
 *  - https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/13673
 *  - https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/22017
 * 
 * 
 * ## Should You Use This Patch?
 * 
 * Decision tree:
 *  - Could you fork OpenCode, patch the source, and recompile it? Yes.
 *  - Should you do that? Yes.
 *  - Are you lazy and want a quick hack? Also yes.
 *  - Does this come with any warranties? Absolutely not.
 *  - Is it safe? Sure. :homer-bush:
 *  - Should you use this? No. Compile from source.
 *  - Can you use it? Yes. Read what it does, and decide for yourself.
 *
 * 
 * ## How This Works
 * 
 * First, see:
 * https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/tui/src/app.tsx
 * 
 * That file does a few things, including (abbreviated) setting up OpenTUI:
 *  - `import { createCliRenderer, MouseButton } from "@opentui/core"`
 *  - `createCliRenderer({ ... targetFps: 60, gatherStats: false, ... })`
 * 
 * In the compiled `opencode` binary, that ends up minified to a single string:
 *  - `targetFps:60,gatherStats:!1`  (27 characters / bytes)
 * 
 * While `targetFps` limits continuous/live rendering,
 * `maxFps` (notably missing) limits immediate `requestRender()` frames.
 * Setting both is required and applies the same cap to both rendering paths.
 * 
 * But `gatherStats` defaults to `false` in OpenTUI. So we don't need that.
 * We overwrite this 27 byte string with a new string of the **same length**,
 * but with our desired FPS and `maxFps` set to the same value.
 * 
 * That is all this patch does. It makes a copy of the `opencode` binary,
 * and overwrites that string with a new one, containing the desired FPS.
 * 
 * 
 * ## How to Use This
 * 
 *  1. Make sure you have Node.js installed.
 *  2. Save this script to a file, e.g. `opencode-fps-patch.js`.
 *  3. Run `node opencode-fps-patch.js <1-99>`,
 *     e.g. `node opencode-fps-patch.js 10`.
 *  4. The new binary is written to,
 *     e.g. `/usr/local/bin/opencode-fps-10`.
 * 
 *
 * ## Which OpenCode Versions is this Compatible With?
 *
 *  - This is a binary patch. 
 *  - This is Linux/Docker oriented; it will not work with signed executables.
 *  - It was tested against the compiled `opencode` in official Docker image:
 *    `ghcr.io/anomalyco/opencode` (originally developed on v1.17.15)
